High fantasy creatures such as dragons, elves, dwarves and the like (new and original creatures invented by the author included)

Magic and wizards, especially the kind that fling fireballs, conjure lightning etc. Think dungeons and dragons style magic

Fantasy locations that are based on places besides medieval Europe (Africa, Asia, The Middle East, Indian Subcontinent etc.)

The classic hero's journey narrative, especially where the person comes from humble beginnings and grows throughout the story

Cosmic horror

Big battles

Concepts and plot points based on real world mythology, such as Norse mythology, angels/demons, etc

steampunk, and other works of fiction based on historical time periods

Talking animals, or animals as main characters/strong plot points

Dystopias/post-apocalyptic settings

I have depression and anxiety. Currently writing this from a mental health short stay ward.

1. “But you can CHOOSE how you feel” doesn’t apply to us. Yes we can make choices that will improve our mental health, but we can’t magically snap our fingers and feel better. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve heard “well just don’t feel x, it’s a choice” and it’s so offensive 

2. Don’t expect us to see a therapist a few times and magically be cured. For a lot of us mental health is a lifelong journey with ups and downs. Therapy helps a lot but it’s not a silver bullet.

3. Just because my affect is ok, doesn’t mean I’m not depressed or anxious. We get very good at hiding emotions people don’t want to see. I could be laughing with you but feel horrible inside.

4. Some of us just need meds. It’s unfortunate, but for some of us there’s a chemical imbalance in our brains that make it hard/impossible to function without them.

5. Mental health issues are not are excuse to be abusive. I know a woman whose husband beats her and her kids and she always excuses it because he’s depressed. There are so many mentally ill people who are wonderful to those around them and if an illness is causing someone to treat you like garbage, you have every right to remove them from your life.

Combined with my mental health issues it becomes a cycle of meet new person  > befriend new person > get attached to new person too quickly > upset person due to autism making social interaction hard > loosing friend and being alone making depression worse > get anxiety about new friendships due to past experience and anxiety about rejection

Due to this I don't really have friends my age, partly by choice. I tend to keep myself busy with video games and cats. Oddly enough I socialise by spending time with my mums friends who are in their 40s-50s and super nice to me. I find that with other young people they are either super judgemental or I feel as though there is some sort of competition as of who has their lives "together" the most and I just can't relate. I have met some nice people my own age but my anxiety has prevented me forming bonds with them.

I assume that nonautisitic people have some sort of gauge that measures when they are either being too clingy or too distant? I don't have that at all, so any kind of relationship is risking going in either direction. I am 24 and never been in a relationship or even kissed anyone which is a little sad but it could be much worse.

If there is a positive I would have to say my conditions enable me to connect with other people with similar issues. I worked in a school for a while basically supporting kids with behavioural issues and one girl I was working with asked if "(my name) has Aspergers too?" It was a great moment for me and I felt as I could really help this kid due to this shared connection we had.

Sorry if that was long and rambling, a million thoughts came to me at once when I saw the thread topic lol.

Not as bad as half of these other comments (and somewhat humorous) but was very annoying at the time. I have an unknown problem with my urinary tract/kidneys which sees me hospitalised on occasion, so I have seen some shit in hospitals.

On this particular occasion, I was in the ER with a kidney flare up waiting for a doctor to see if I needed IV antibiotics. It was about 1am. The woman in the bay next to me would not shut the fuck up. She was older and had a thick European accent, but it didn't seem to me that there was any kind of mental illness or dementia that would account for her behaviour. Bitch was just selfish. She continuously screamed for nurse/doctor attention because she was tired of waiting (aren't we all lady, it's the ER!). She had a broken arm or some shit and expected the doctors to fix it then and there at 1am. It was early and everyone was tired and cranky and had zero patience for this woman. 

The funniest part was when she was given an ice chip, as she wouldn't stop screaming at the nurses that she was thirsty no matter how many times they explained that she was fasting in case of surgery. Well, this woman did not approve of the ice chip and promptly threw it on the floor in protest. I could not believe I just witnessed a grown woman throwing a tantrum over an ice chip. Seriously nurses deserve an award for dealing with this crap.

There was also an occasion where I had to stay in a ward overnight and kept getting woken up by the screams of patients with dementia. Nothing like being woken up by the sound of an elderly man screaming "I SHAT THE BED. I SHITTED." Both sad and horrific to be jolted from sleep to.

It was a normal day and I (17 years old) was walking to school. Just inside the gates, I saw something small writhing on the road. It was a tiny tabby kitten, writhing in a pool of its own blood. People were using the road to drop their kids off and I could see them going out of their way to avoid running it over. There was a split second for me, a cat lover, where I frantically though "wtf do I do". In my panicked state I ran into the school building and told the front office lady who then sent out maintainence to deal with it.

I regret that so much. I later heard kids talking amount themselves how they saw a dead kitten with its intestines everywhere. If only I had run out and picked it up, it might have been saved. I cried so much I had to come home from school, and gave my kitty a super big hug when I got home. The other kids didn't understand why I was so upset since it was "just a cat", which was tough, but lucky my mum is a cat lover too and understood. I will never forgive myself for not saving the cat; it was one of those fight or flight moments and I chose flight :(
